terms.grammar: imperative of abeō (or ī) with in malam crucem, “to an evil cross”
evidence: Plaut. Most. 3.2.163: abin hinc in malam crucem? (Lewis & Short), s.v. abeō
terms.comment: A curse of comedy: the cross was the slave’s punishment. Lewis & Short: “go to the devil! go and be hanged!”. Also abī in malam rem! (Plaut. Pers. 2.4.17).

terms.latin: Ī dierēctē in maximam malam crucem!
terms.gloss: go and hang yourself, the higher the better!
evidence: Plaut. Poen. 1.2.134: ī dierēctē in maxumam malam crucem (Lewis & Short), s.v. dierēctus
terms.comment: Traupman prints dīrēctē; the word in Plautus is dierēctē, of uncertain meaning (Lewis & Short s.v. dierēctus).

sources: Lewis & Short: crux · Lewis & Short: abeo · Lewis & Short: dierectus
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 100, checked against the searchable text and the page image (12 November 2026).
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
